message.content:
This looks like a CBP ruling on a self-adhesive PVC gel mat used at a workstation. I think it was classified in heading 3918 (floor coverings of plastics, whether or not self-adhesive, in rolls or tiles) or 3926. A 9x9 inch square mat is a tile-like shape, but it is used as a workstation mat rather than as a floor covering. Heading 3918 covers floor coverings and wall or ceiling coverings, so a workstation mat does not fit well.

The alternatives are 3919 (self-adhesive plates, sheets, film, and other flat shapes of plastics) or 3926.90. The product is a gel mat with release paper, which suggests a self-adhesive flat shape and so 3919. However, 3919 is for flat shapes in rolls or not, and the gel mat is used as a mat, which is a finished article. Heading 3926 also covers other articles of plastics, and 3926.90.99 is the generic subheading, so that is plausible.

On balance I'll go with 3926.90.9989 (other articles of plastics, other, other). The old statistical suffix was 3926.90.9990 and later became 3926.90.99 with 10-digit splits such as 3926.90.9910 and 3926.90.9980/9989. Since 3926.90.9989 is a current "other" line, I'll use that.

{"hts_code": "3926.90.9989", "reason": "A finished self-adhesive PVC gel workstation mat is an article of plastics not elsewhere specified, so it falls in the residual heading 3926 \"other articles of plastics\" rather than the floor-covering or flat-shape headings."}
